paragraphs.name: a998
paragraphs.text: Stop Clicking Through Android Traces — Use SQL to Find Jank in 30 Seconds

paragraphs.name: 3c4d
paragraphs.text: The complete Perfetto SQL handbook for CPU, memory, rendering, binder, and jank investigations on Android, TV, and Fire TV.

paragraphs.name: 7a4a
paragraphs.text: Production jank report lands in your inbox at 11 PM. Users are reporting stutter during scroll. You pull a trace, open Perfetto UI, and stare at 12,000 horizontal slices across 40 threads.

paragraphs.name: 89f1
paragraphs.text: You start clicking. You zoom in on a long slice. You zoom out. You click something else. Forty minutes later you haven’t found the root cause.
That’s not debugging. That’s archaeology.

paragraphs.name: a59d
paragraphs.text: After 8 years building Android apps across phones, TV, STB, and Firestick, I can tell you the single biggest shift in my performance workflow wasn’t a new profiler or a faster device — it was treating Perfetto as a database.

paragraphs.name: ef8d
paragraphs.text: Every CPU state change, every binder call, every frame drop, every GC pause — it’s all in SQL tables. Once you start querying instead of clicking, a 40-minute investigation becomes a 30-second query. This article is the handbook I wish I’d had from the start.

paragraphs.name: fd8a
paragraphs.text: The most effective debugging tool is still careful thought, coupled with judiciously placed print statements. — Brian Kernighan, The Practice of Programming
